title: Serving Web from volatile Dial-up IP
excerpt: My homelab is behind a dial-up IP link with occasional unexpected reconnects. There is dynamic DNS, but I prefer a reverse proxy between me and the bots.
content_html:
A.S.: it's actually not dial-up, but a volatile IP, typical for DSL home routers.

My homelab is behind a dial-up IP link with occasional unexpected reconnects.

There is dynamic DNS, but I prefer a reverse proxy[1] between the bots and me. And dyndns doesn't notify other servers (the reverse proxy).

No push? Then poll.

There's a cron-job on the homelab server triggering a refresh of the reverse proxy cfg if the IP has changed:

# note: no sudo
$ crontab -l
*/15   *       *       *       *       .local/bin/http-up.sh snac.mro.name    vps.mro.name /var/www/vhosts/snac.mro.name/proxy-dyndns.conf

with a (local) script doing the heavy lifting (shell escaping mostly):

#!/bin/sh

[ "$3" = "" ] && {
  cat <<EOFz

Check if localhost can curl an url and if not, envsubst the current IP as \$IPv4
into a (remote) reverse proxy config in case & reload (lighttpd).

SYNOPSIS

  \$ $0 <http url> <ssh host> <reverse proxy cfg file>

EOFz
  exit 0
}

curl \
  --fail \
  --location \
  --max-time 3.1 \
  --output /dev/null \
  --silent \
  "$1" \
&& exit 0

ssh -4 "$2" \
  "IPv4=\$(echo \$SSH_CLIENT | cut -d ' ' -f 1) envsubst \
   < \"$3.tpl\" \
   > \"$3\"
  sudo service lighttpd reload
  ls -l \"$3\" "

After DSL reconnects, the server comes back online with the new IP within the next 15 minutes - fine for me. No other parties involved and the volatile host notifies the passive reverse proxy.

And: I can make do with cron & ssh and need no other tools or services.
